My most recent model is the Flexcare. Philips sent me a HydroClean brush head to try out. I had been using the ProResults brush head and I had found it to be a big improvement over prior models, primarily because of its smaller size. I assume they manufactured it this way to make up for my second reason. Second, the brush head has had the center bristles removed to add the gimmicky rubber channels meant to direct the water/toothpaste between teeth. This is Philips' best brush head yet. The smaller profile is much better at cleaning hard-to-reach places. While I can't really say I felt water and toothpaste being directed between my teeth, the HydroGuides definitely feel great along my gums.  To the previous reviewer: of course you still have to floss! The product description never claims you don't have to floss; it says "...get closer to the benefits of flossing". reviews.t: Marketing gimmick - Stick to ProResults heads
reviews.x: I bought this brush, hoping it would perform as stated.  However, when I used it, I didn't any positive effects of the "hydroclean" design.  What I did notice was this:  -It was hard to brush my teeth with that annoying rubber thing sticking out -The bristles themselves were firmer than the ProResults brush heads -There were less bristles because of the rubber in the middle -No noticeable "directing of fluids" between my teeth.  Think about it:  The only way this would work is if there was a lar

This is a nice improvement to the Sonicare line of brushes. It appears to be their response to the Oral-B Floss Action line of brushes that have a "paddle" to help get between teeth. This accomplishes that goal with an plastic insert in the middle that helps direct the toothpaste between your teeth.  I use both the Sonicare (Healthy White) and the Oral B 5000. Both have their pluses and minuses, so switching between the two gives me the best of both worlds.  The Oral-B arrangement of paddles doe

I'm so glad that amazon has these, just one came with my handle along with two standard heads. I used the standard first and just switched it out with the hydro... love how it feels on my teeth and gums! And this is a great price. I normally get the replacement heads at costco but they only have the standards. I agree that you shouldn't think this replaces flossing, but it sure feels like it does more than the standard brush.

The paddles push toothpaste foam between your teeth.  If you brush behind your teeth while looking in the mirror, you can see the foam bubbling out between your teeth.  Brushing the front of your teeth, you can feel the foam flowing out behind your teeth with your tongue.  Move the brush very slowly along the gum line.  Rapid movements upset the flow and are  counterproductive.  Also, be sure you use a toothpaste that makes lots of foam.  Push the foam back to the brush with your tongue so the f

After getting our new Healthy White SoniCare, we needed another brush head. The only ones I found while out shopping which fit the Healthy White, were the HydroClean brush heads. I don't care for these at all, since there is a thin row of bristles on the outsides. They are also scratchy on the gums. I much prefer the ProResults brush heads and would order online if need be (just to avoid the HydroClean type).

This is useless. Still have to floss, no difference. Besides, those "specially designed paddles" hit teeth much harder and more painful than bristles. I did not notice any direction of fluids between teeth. Waste of money

I have been a fan of Sonicare for about 10 years.  In April, I needed to order some replacements heads for my unit.  Pros: - Cons:  Since there are a limited number of brushes it seems as if they are stronger and often cut into my gums.  I have had this happen numerous times on all three in the package.  Also - it seems as the "blue bristles" change color rather quick.  In fact, mine were halfway worn after the first two weeks.  Overall, I would recommend that you stick with basic replacement he

Compared to my regular replacement heads, these heads feel much firmer and more stimulating to the gum.  They also snap more firmly to my brush than do my regular heads and run more quietly.  If I had to choose between the two, I'd choose my regular head first.  Because, however, I've already bought these and they may have some beneficial effects the regular heads lack, I've chosen to alternate the heads.  I use one head to clean my teeth with baking soda, then floss, then use the other head to

The primary difference between these HydroClean heads and a full-size SoniCare head is that Philips has replaced all of the bristles in the center with two little rubber flaps.  If my own experience is any indication, it's a poor trade-off.  Within just a couple weeks of switching to this new head, I'm seeing a lot of buildup on my teeth... which does not occur with the original style heads unless they are overdue for replacement.  I'm switching back!
These work great if you have a small mouth or trouble getting to your back teeth.

Their is nothing wrong with the way that the brush heads worked, they were not very soft, which is the type of brush head that I was looking for, if you are looking for soft brush heads these are not it, but if you want medium brush heads these will work fine for you I'm sure. That is the reason for the 4 star review.

These are harder than Sonicare's regular brushes and harder than I prefer.  I noticed no difference in how clean my teeth felt or looked.  I floss regularly and I don't think directing a flow of water can do the same job of removing debris, so for me, directing water between my teeth probably doesn't do much except make it easier to accidentally splatter.  I also missed the inner rows of brushes that the rubber paddles replace and I know I felt the difference.  Unless I see some hard evidence to

I decided to try these new fangled brush heads just to see what they were all about... The center "paddle" seemed to be doing its job of directing water and toothpaste between my teeth, but it felt like it was a tad too long and hard, causing some discomfort on the gums.  Maybe just something to get used to... However, comparing side by side the new heads and the old brush heads, I still prefer the feeling of the old ones.

...I can't tell the difference as far as the claim that it "directs fluids between teeth" but it does clean my teeth very well. The only problem I have with these replacement heads is that the color bands don't fit on the base of the brush head like it does on the original so it slides around on the base unit. NOT cool!! I think they forgot to design in a boss or lip or whatever to hold the color band securely.

reviews.t: These are what I would consider to be the best brush heads for the Sonicare toothbrush that I've used ...
reviews.x: These are what I would consider to be the best brush heads for the Sonicare toothbrush that I've used however; it would appear that Phillips is phasing these out for other models. If you can still find them, they are a good initial method of cleaning your teeth prior to flossing.

reviews.t: All brushes are the same color
reviews.x: This is a ridiculous product.  My partner and I share the sonicare.  But, for these replacemments, all the brushes are the same color so there's no way to know whose brush is whose.
These were hard to find as they appear to be discontinued.  I got them for my daughter to help keep her braces clean.  Work like a charm!

reviews.t: Almost as good as my Ultreo.
reviews.x: The Ultreo was the best toothbrush I have ever had. But it had a bad failing, the rechargeable batteries in the handle were of poor quality and not replaceable. During Ultreo's short life, they sent me three replacement handles. When the company failed, i bought a bunch of replacement brushes. But the handle soon failed again. But I was able to sell my extra brushes on eBay for a very tidy sum. Next I bought the Sonicare, it was quite good. But when I got the new HydroClean brush heads, I realiz

I love the sonic care toothbrush period. Yet the hype for this brush head was short lived for me. I just don't feel any difference with this and the original. It brushes just as good though with the two paddles in the middle it almost feels like I'm missing some important scrubbing power on my teeth. I floss like normal with Crest Glide comfort plus, so the need to have a brush that "flosses" is not really needed. But hey Amazon just has wonderful prices on these brush heads. There is no reason

This product is absolutely amazing! This tooth brush head is the best ever and I don't think I would go back to a standard tooth brush head again. From the first time you use the HydroClean you can feel a difference! Cleaner, fresher, smoother teeth that last a lot longer because you seem to be removing more plaque from your teeth with each use. I completely recommend the Philips Sonicare Hydro Clean tooth brush heads to anyone wanting a fresh feeling mouth!

reviews.t: Great Product...heads only, not the brush.
reviews.x: The heads are fine, but following is my review of the brush itself:  It was a good brush while it worked, but entirely too expensive. I understand it's important to take care of our teeth, but this brush lasted 2 1/2 yrs. and cost about $400. (original unit, plus replacement heads). I'm now looking at powered brushes for under $20. that can be tossed when they eventually fail. I figure at that price I can get 20+ yrs. out of them for $400.

reviews.t: Glad to have bought this!! Fresh and So Clean!
reviews.x: I just received the pack today and I have to say the the first time brushing it felt great. I'm not sure that it was because I hadn't had a new brush on it for a while but the old one was not getting it clean (the bigger one my brush came with). But it works great. Clean...very very clean and smooth I would recommend these as there's not too much difference in the price between the 3 different models. Using a FlexCare+.

claims.text: Many reviewers find the brush heads too firm or hard, not soft as they prefer.
Several reviewers report no noticeable cleaning difference or benefit from the HydroClean design.
Some reviewers praise the smaller profile and find it effective for hard-to-reach areas and feels great on teeth and gums.
Some reviewers describe the rubber paddles/flaps as uncomfortable, scratchy, or painful on teeth and gums.
A few reviewers appreciate the design that helps direct toothpaste foam between teeth.
